claims.text: Wat Pho is one of Bangkok's oldest temples, originally named Wat Photaram in reference to the sacred monastery of the Bodhi tree in India.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: It is ranked as the highest grade of the first-class royal temples in Thailand and became the main temple of King Rama I.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: In 1788, the king ordered the rebuilding of the dilapidated site and initiated a massive project to rescue and enshrine abandoned Buddha images from across the country.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: Today, the complex houses the largest collection of Buddha images in Thailand, most notably an enormous reclining Buddha measuring 46 metres in length.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: Considered the earliest centre for public education in the country, the temple is widely celebrated as the historic birthplace of traditional Thai massage.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: Fascinating educational illustrations and inscriptions covering various subjects were placed around the complex and have since been recognised by the UNESCO Memory of the World Programme.
claims.subject: self
